city.name: Tokyo
city.description: Marunouchi to Tokyo Tower from open data, lit by the real sun. Every building height is a PLATEAU survey value, and every shadow is computed.

tour.title: Marunouchi to Tokyo Tower, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height that Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI 5 m laser-scanned bare earth under GSI aerial photos.

tour.title: Tokyo Station and the air above it
tour.text: Tokyo Station's red-brick Marunouchi building was restored in 2012. The unused floor area above it was sold to the towers around it, so the old station stays low while Marunouchi grows tall. Compare it with JP Tower, behind it, at 200 m.

tour.title: Hibiya Park at lunch
tour.text: On the winter solstice, {sun:Hibiya Park 日比谷公園|12-22|12:00}% of Hibiya Park is in direct sun at noon, and {sun:Hibiya Park 日比谷公園|12-22|13:00}% at 13:00. On 21 June at noon it is {sun:Hibiya Park 日比谷公園|6-21|12:00}%. No rule protects either.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: surveyed height (PLATEAU or OpenStreetMap). Orange: floor count. Green: estimated. In the model, PLATEAU's roof surveys give every tower in Marunouchi, Shiodome and Toranomon its real massing, podium and all.

tour.title: Tokyo Tower at sunset
tour.text: 333 m, painted in bands of International Orange and white because aircraft must see it. The lattice is built from published dimensions, anchored at the tower's published coordinates.

tour.title: After dark
tour.text: Windows light from the same facade grid that shades them by day. Drag to explore, or open Sun access to test a tower of your own.

protection.title: No sun-access rule: a lunch-hour test
protection.summary: Tokyo has no rule that protects sun on parks and plazas. The windows here are a thought experiment for this project: what would a new tower cost the lunch hour?
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. Tokyo's shadow rule, 日影規制 (Building Standards Act, art. 56-2), limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in designated residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Marunouchi. Check the ward's zoning before relying on this.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year (no daylight saving), so the clock and the sun agree all year. Baseline: the test compares against today's PLATEAU model, which is surveyed to 2020-ish, so towers built since are missing from 76% of the footprint area's heights unless Overture or OSM has them.
protection.tip: Tip: try the block south-west of Hibiya Park, or between the Marunouchi towers and the Palace.
